core.title: Supported
core.definition: Positive runtime evidence confirms the exact reported capability or queried combination.
core.detail: Support is scoped to the exact query; it is never inferred from a GPU marketing name.

core.title: Unsupported
core.definition: Explicit runtime evidence proves the exact capability or queried combination is not supported.
core.detail: A negative result for one tuple/profile does not automatically make a broader feature or format unsupported.

core.title: Unavailable
core.definition: The query could not produce usable capability evidence.
core.detail: Unavailable is not proof of unsupported hardware; failures, timeouts, incomplete prerequisites or inaccessible paths can produce it.

core.title: Not applicable
core.definition: A prerequisite, API scope or extension is not exposed, so that query does not apply to the selected runtime path.
core.detail: For example, Vulkan Video being Not applicable does not prove hardware video decode/encode is absent; it describes only the Vulkan Video API path of the selected Vulkan driver.

core.title: Unknown
core.definition: There is not enough authoritative evidence to classify the capability.
core.detail: Unknown is intentionally distinct from Unsupported and from Not applicable.

core.title: Vulkan instance
core.definition: VkInstance is the application-level connection to a Vulkan implementation.
core.detail: Instance extensions/layers and the instance API version define what can be requested before selecting a physical device.

core.title: Physical device
core.definition: VkPhysicalDevice represents a Vulkan-capable implementation/device discovered from an instance.
core.detail: Features, properties, limits, memory types, queues, formats and extension enumeration are primarily queried from this object.

core.title: Logical device
core.definition: VkDevice is the application-created logical interface to one selected physical device.
core.detail: Enabled device features/extensions and queues become usable through this object; enumeration alone does not enable them.

core.title: Queue
core.definition: VkQueue is an execution/presentation queue obtained from a logical device.
core.detail: Queue-family flags describe what kinds of work can be submitted; presentation support is Surface-specific evidence.

core.title: Command buffer
core.definition: VkCommandBuffer records Vulkan commands for later submission to a queue.
core.detail: Most vkCmd* calls record work; they do not execute GPU work at the moment the function is called.

core.title: Feature
core.definition: A Vulkan feature is usually a Boolean capability that must be queried and, when required, enabled before use.
core.detail: Feature structs often participate in extensible pNext chains.

core.title: Property
core.definition: A property is implementation information such as supported modes, identifiers, alignments or behavioral characteristics.
core.detail: Properties describe the implementation; they are not normally enabled like Boolean features.

core.title: Limit
core.definition: A limit is a numeric boundary such as a maximum size/count or required alignment.
core.detail: The comparison direction matters: some requirements need at least a value, while others require not exceeding a maximum.

core.title: Format
core.definition: VkFormat identifies an image/buffer element format.
core.detail: Format support depends on tiling, usage and feature flags; a single failed tuple must not be generalized into universal format unsupported status.

core.title: Layer
core.definition: A Vulkan layer can intercept Vulkan calls to provide validation, tooling or other behavior.
core.detail: Layer presence is separate from device capability support.

core.title: Extension
core.definition: An extension adds Vulkan API functionality outside a particular core-version baseline.
core.detail: Being registered by Khronos is reference metadata; runtime support requires authoritative enumeration/query evidence.

core.title: Surface / WSI
core.definition: VkSurfaceKHR represents a platform presentation target; WSI means Window System Integration.
core.detail: Surface formats, present modes, capabilities and presentation-queue support depend on the live Surface and can change with it.

core.title: Swapchain
core.definition: VkSwapchainKHR manages presentable images associated with a Surface.
core.detail: VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR can remain usable, while VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR requires re-query/recreation before successful presentation can continue.

core.title: pNext
core.definition: pNext links extensible Vulkan structures into input/output chains.
core.detail: Each chained structure must use the correct sType; VulkanScope uses validated chains rather than guessing unsupported structures.

core.title: sType
core.definition: sType identifies the concrete Vulkan structure type to the implementation.
core.detail: It is normally set to the corresponding VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_* enumerant before the structure is passed to Vulkan.

core.title: Loader API version
core.definition: The highest Vulkan API version reported by the Vulkan loader entry-point path.
core.detail: It is not the same as a physical device's API version or the driver version.

core.title: Device API version
core.definition: The Vulkan core API version exposed by a particular VkPhysicalDevice.
core.detail: Core feature/property query eligibility follows this runtime device version plus relevant extension exposure.

core.title: Driver version
core.definition: A vendor/driver-specific version value associated with the selected physical device.
core.detail: Its encoding can be vendor-specific and must not be confused with Vulkan core API version.

core.title: vk* command
core.definition: Vulkan commands use a lowercase vk prefix followed by an action/object name, for example vkCreateInstance or vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2.
core.detail: The command's returned VkResult, if any, reports that operation's status rather than a global device verdict.

core.title: vkCmd* command
core.definition: vkCmd* commands record operations into a VkCommandBuffer.
core.detail: Recording generally defers execution until the command buffer is submitted to an appropriate queue.

core.title: vkQueue* command
core.definition: vkQueue* commands act directly on a VkQueue, such as submitting work or presenting.
core.detail: Queue-family capabilities and any Surface-specific presentation evidence still constrain valid use.

core.title: Vk* type
core.definition: Vk* names are Vulkan types: handles, structures, enums, bitmasks, aliases and related API types.
core.detail: Structure names do not themselves prove that a runtime supports the feature represented by that structure.

core.title: VK_* token
core.definition: VK_* names are Vulkan constants, enumerants, bit flags, result codes, structure-type identifiers, extension-name macros and other registered tokens.
core.detail: A _BIT token is normally a bitflag value; vendor/KHR/EXT suffixes identify the namespace that introduced the token.

core.title: VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_*
core.definition: A VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_* enumerant is the sType discriminator for a Vulkan structure.
core.detail: It lets the implementation identify the concrete structure in ordinary arguments and pNext chains.

core.title: *_BIT
core.definition: Names ending in _BIT (before any vendor suffix) are bitflag enumerants intended to be combined in compatible flag fields.
core.detail: A zero-valued *_NONE name means no bits are selected rather than a capability bit.

core.title: KHR / EXT / vendor suffix
core.definition: KHR identifies Khronos extensions, EXT identifies multi-vendor extensions, while tags such as AMD, NV, QCOM, ARM or INTEL identify vendor namespaces.
core.detail: A suffix records API namespace/provenance; it is not runtime support evidence.

vkResults.name: VK_SUCCESS
vkResults.meaning: Command successfully completed. This is success for that command only, not global capability evidence.

vkResults.name: VK_NOT_READY
vkResults.meaning: A fence or query has not completed yet; the operation can be checked again later.

vkResults.name: VK_TIMEOUT
vkResults.meaning: A wait operation did not finish within the requested timeout interval.

vkResults.name: VK_EVENT_SET
vkResults.meaning: The queried Vulkan event is currently signaled.

vkResults.name: VK_EVENT_RESET
vkResults.meaning: The queried Vulkan event is currently unsignaled.

vkResults.name: VK_INCOMPLETE
vkResults.meaning: A return array was too small for the complete result. Partial positive data may still be retained, but absence must not be inferred.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY
vkResults.meaning: A CPU/host-side memory allocation required by the Vulkan operation failed.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY
vkResults.meaning: A device/GPU memory allocation required by the Vulkan operation failed.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED
vkResults.meaning: An object could not be initialized for an implementation-specific reason.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST
vkResults.meaning: The logical or physical device was lost. Existing work may no longer complete and the device generally has to be recreated.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_MEMORY_MAP_FAILED
vkResults.meaning: Mapping a Vulkan memory object into host address space failed.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_LAYER_NOT_PRESENT
vkResults.meaning: A requested Vulkan layer is unavailable or could not be loaded.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_EXTENSION_NOT_PRESENT
vkResults.meaning: A requested Vulkan extension is not exposed by the implementation for that creation/use path.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT
vkResults.meaning: A requested Vulkan feature is not supported for the attempted operation.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER
vkResults.meaning: The requested Vulkan API/version is incompatible with the available driver implementation.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_TOO_MANY_OBJECTS
vkResults.meaning: The implementation cannot create another object of the requested type because an object-count limit was reached.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED
vkResults.meaning: The exact requested format/use combination is not supported. VulkanScope never expands this into a broader format-wide claim.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_FRAGMENTED_POOL
vkResults.meaning: A pool allocation failed specifically because the pool's available memory is fragmented.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN
vkResults.meaning: An unexpected runtime failure occurred that Vulkan cannot classify more specifically.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED
vkResults.meaning: Invalid Vulkan usage was detected by an implementation or validation layer and the command failed.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY
vkResults.meaning: A pool allocation failed because the pool cannot satisfy the request.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INVALID_EXTERNAL_HANDLE
vkResults.meaning: An imported/exported external handle is not valid for the requested Vulkan handle type.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INVALID_OPAQUE_CAPTURE_ADDRESS
vkResults.meaning: A requested opaque capture/device address or related captured handle information is no longer valid or available.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_FRAGMENTATION
vkResults.meaning: Creation failed because the relevant allocation space is too fragmented.

vkResults.name: VK_PIPELINE_COMPILE_REQUIRED
vkResults.meaning: Pipeline creation would require compilation, but the application requested a path that does not perform that compilation.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED
vkResults.meaning: The implementation denied a privileged request, such as acquiring a higher global queue priority.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The presentation surface is no longer available and must be recreated before presentation can continue.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_NATIVE_WINDOW_IN_USE_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The native window is already in use in a way that prevents Vulkan from using it for this surface operation.

vkResults.name: VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR
vkResults.meaning: Presentation can still succeed, but the swapchain no longer matches the surface properties exactly.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The surface changed and the swapchain is no longer compatible. Surface properties must be queried again and the swapchain recreated.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DISPLAY_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The display and swapchain/image presentation configuration are incompatible for the requested operation.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INVALID_SHADER_NV
vkResults.meaning: One or more shaders failed the implementation's compile/link validation for this NVIDIA extension path.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_IMAGE_USAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The requested image usage flags are not supported for the exact Vulkan Video/image query.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_VIDEO_PICTURE_LAYOUT_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The requested Vulkan Video picture layout is not supported.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_VIDEO_PROFILE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The video codec operation selected by the exact video profile is not supported.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_VIDEO_PROFILE_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The format parameters in the exact Vulkan Video profile chain are not supported.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_VIDEO_PROFILE_CODEC_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: Codec-specific parameters in the exact Vulkan Video profile chain are not supported.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_VIDEO_STD_VERSION_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The requested Vulkan Video standard-header version is not supported.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INVALID_DRM_FORMAT_MODIFIER_PLANE_LAYOUT_EXT
vkResults.meaning: The supplied DRM format-modifier plane layout is invalid for the requested image configuration.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_PRESENT_TIMING_QUEUE_FULL_EXT
vkResults.meaning: The swapchain's present-timing results queue has insufficient space for another requested timing record.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_FULL_SCREEN_EXCLUSIVE_MODE_LOST_EXT
vkResults.meaning: An operation requiring application-controlled exclusive full-screen access failed because that exclusivity was lost.

vkResults.name: VK_THREAD_IDLE_KHR
vkResults.meaning: A deferred operation is unfinished, but this thread currently has no work available to perform.

vkResults.name: VK_THREAD_DONE_KHR
vkResults.meaning: A deferred operation is unfinished, but there is no more work to assign to additional threads.

vkResults.name: VK_OPERATION_DEFERRED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: A deferred-host operation was requested and at least part of its work was actually deferred.

vkResults.name: VK_OPERATION_NOT_DEFERRED_KHR
vkResults.meaning: A deferred-host operation was requested, but no part of the work was deferred.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_INVALID_VIDEO_STD_PARAMETERS_KHR
vkResults.meaning: Video-standard parameters are syntactically/semantically invalid or exceed the codec/implementation capabilities for that exact request.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_COMPRESSION_EXHAUSTED_EXT
vkResults.meaning: Image creation with requested fixed-rate compression failed because the implementation's compression resources are exhausted.

vkResults.name: VK_INCOMPATIBLE_SHADER_BINARY_EXT
vkResults.meaning: The supplied binary shader code is not compatible with this device.

vkResults.name: VK_PIPELINE_BINARY_MISSING_KHR
vkResults.meaning: A requested pipeline binary was not found in the implementation's internal cache.

vkResults.name: VK_ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_SPACE_KHR
vkResults.meaning: The caller did not provide enough output space for all required returned data.

commonCommands.vkEnumerateInstanceVersion: Reports the highest Vulkan core API version supported by the loader path.
commonCommands.vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties: Enumerates instance extensions exposed by the loader/implementation for the requested layer scope.
commonCommands.vkCreateInstance: Creates a VkInstance using the requested application API version, layers and instance extensions.
commonCommands.vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices: Enumerates VkPhysicalDevice handles available to a Vulkan instance.
commonCommands.vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties: Enumerates device extensions exposed by a selected physical device.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2: Queries core and pNext-chained physical-device feature structures without enabling them.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2: Queries core and pNext-chained physical-device properties/limits/identifiers.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties2: Queries memory heaps, memory types and pNext extension memory properties.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties: Queries queue-family counts, flags and pNext queue-family properties.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceFormatProperties2: Queries format feature support, including extensible 64-bit format-feature data when exposed.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties: Tests an exact image type/format/tiling/usage/flags tuple and returns image-format properties when supported.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR: Tests whether one queue family can present to one concrete VkSurfaceKHR.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKH: Queries presentation capabilities for a concrete Surface.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceFormatsKHR: Enumerates format/color-space pairs supported for a concrete Surface.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfacePresentModesKH: Enumerates present modes supported for a concrete Surface.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoCapabilitiesKHR: Queries capabilities for one exact Vulkan Video profile chain; success must not be generalized to every codec/profile combination.
commonCommands.vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoFormatProperties: Enumerates video format properties for a specified Vulkan Video profile/usage query.
